answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the prism ordering is published with the spiral batch, the onyx audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 36% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 177 account operation therefore ties up 17 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
